title: FlashFusion throughput edgecases worklog
content:
Objective:
- Track a set of reproducible microbenchmarks where fused kernels (kernel-fusion + FlashAttention paths) unexpectedly regress or show non-monotonic throughput when sequence length or batch composition changes.

Context / motivation:
- We ship automatic kernel selection in the runtime that picks between FlashAttention2, paged-attention fallback, and a fused-attention kernel we maintain. In production we observed two classes of anomalies:
  1) sudden throughput cliffs at particular sequence-length boundaries (e.g., throughput drop at 768->800 tokens)
  2) noisy p99s and occasional long-tail latencies when mixing short and long requests in the same worker queue.
- Need a disciplined lab notebook to capture reproducible experiments, heuristics, and a concrete plan to harden kernel selection.

Hardware / baseline environment used for tests:
- GPU: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB (dev cluster), CUDA 12.1, cuBLAS 12.1, cuDNN 9.1
- Driver: 535.113
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04, kernel 6.1
- Runtime build: serving-runtime main @ commit ab12cde (2025-02-05) with kernel-selector toggles
- Models: llama-2-13b (fp16), local quantized variant q4_0 (for some experiments)
- Test harness: perf/bench/attn_microbench.py (see linked GH PR)

Microbench specification (repro):
- Sequence lengths: [64, 128, 256, 512, 768, 800, 1024, 1536]
- Batch sizes: [1, 2, 4, 8, 16] (priority: 1,4,8)
- Warmup iterations: 60; measure iterations: 600; measure both throughput (tokens/s) and latency distribution (p50, p95, p99).
- Mix tests: 50/50 mix of short(64) and long(1024) within same worker queue; probability-driven arrival to emulate production mix.
- Metric capture: nvprof-style kernel timings + our tracebench timeline (kernel launch times, memcpy sizes, kernel name).

Quick findings (summary):
- FlashAttention2 path: excellent steady throughput for uniform batches, but shows kernel-launch variance and up to +18% p99 increases when mixed with long/short jobs in same process.
- Fused-kernel (our in-house fusion): slightly better peak tokens/s at 512-768 in large batches, but exhibits cliff at ~800 where register pressure changes and a fallback path triggers heavy scratchpad spills.
- Paged-attention fallback: stable memory footprint, but lower tokens/s; however when fusion spills happen it becomes the safer choice and avoids 10-30ms latency spikes.

Detailed notes and traces (examples):
- Repro case A: batch=4, seq=768, model=llama-2-13b/fp16, kernel-selector prioritized fusion -> throughput=67k tok/s, p99=9.4ms.
- Repro case B: batch=4, seq=800, same config -> throughput dropped to 42k tok/s, p99=32ms.
- Trace shows: at 800 tokens our fused kernel switches to a multi-pass reduction (due to exceeding tiling threshold), producing 2x extra global memory writes and a long kernel with 2.8ms and 18ms components.
- Kernel log snippet (simplified):
  - fused_attn_tile_kernels: launch N=3, times=[2.8ms, 18.0ms, 2.9ms]
  - flashattn_forward: launch N=1, time=1.2ms
  - memcpy_device_to_host (small): 0.03ms

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Fusion tiling threshold is set too aggressively and doesn't account for small increases in sequence length that change register usage and force a less efficient schedule.
2) KV prefetch sizing combined with the existing scheduler causes oscillation when large and small requests share a worker due to cache-line thrash in L2/shared memory.
3) Launch overheads for multi-stage fused kernels are non-negligible on the chosen GPU configuration, creating amplification when mixed workloads increase scheduler churn.

Immediate experiments to validate hypotheses (short-term):
- A: Sweep fusion-tiling parameters (tile_m, tile_n) around current values at seq=760..840 and capture register usage and smem consumption. Compare kernel binary register allocation from nvdisasm.
- B: Run single-worker isolation test that injects short jobs between long jobs with and without KV prefetch enabled to see if p99 spikes correlate with prefetch writes.
- C: Disable fusion for sequences above 768 in kernel-selector and run end-to-end stability test (48h) on staging traffic replay to validate fallbacks reduce p99 spikes.

Longer-term mitigations and engineering ideas:
- Improve kernel-selector heuristic: incorporate a cheap model of register pressure and expected multi-pass count rather than just seq length and batch. Cache these heuristics per-model+shape.
- Add a scheduling fence that isolates long-running multi-stage kernels from short low-latency kernels (soft QoS within worker). For example, put long requests into a separate cooperative queue that uses a different GPU stream.
- Enhance fusion kernel codegen to emit a preflight-sanity pass that estimates per-thread reg usage and returns an early signal to runtime to avoid pathological schedules.
- KV-prefetch adaptive sizing: measure inter-arrival distribution and temper prefetch aggressiveness when variance is high.

Notes to self / operational checklist:
- When filing a repo PR, include the failing trace and the bench script seed for reproducibility.
- Add the 800 token repro case to the nightly regression suite as a canary for fusion.
- Capture full GPU timelines with TraceBench and upload to GH artifact for review.
- Engage with perf infra to add 'mixed-size' workload simulation to the CI perf lanes.

Unresolved questions / things to ask the team:
- Do we have a reliable way to read kernel register allocation at runtime for arbitrary JITed kernels? (If not, fallback to nvdisasm offline sampling.)
- Should default kernel-selector thresholds be per-instance (customer) or per-model? My leaning: per-model+shape.
- Are we comfortable adding a short/long request QoS path inside the same worker, or prefer isolating by worker type?

Next steps (owner assignments):
- Marcus: run the tile parameter sweep and paste artifacts under GH PR #842 (due 2025-02-20).
- Sophie: implement a temporary kernel-selector guard that disables fusion for seq>768 and run 48h replay (due 2025-02-24).
- Daniel: craft a TraceBench upload script and add the 800-token case to nightly suite (due 2025-02-28).
- Ava (me): consolidate results and propose runtime heuristic updates by 2025-03-07.

Appendix: commands used (examples)
- python perf/bench/attn_microbench.py --model llama-2-13b --seq 800 --batch 4 --warmup 60 --iters 600 --kernel-selector=auto --trace=trace_800.json
- CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 nv-nsight-cu-cli --target-processes all --section SASS --export greptrace.sass python perf/bench/attn_microbench.py ...

Quick raw numbers table (example runs, median of 5):
- seq 512 bs4 fusion: 91k tok/s, p99 6.1ms
- seq 768 bs4 fusion: 67k tok/s, p99 9.4ms
- seq 800 bs4 fusion: 42k tok/s, p99 32ms
- seq 800 bs4 flashattn: 58k tok/s, p99 10.8ms
- mix short/long 50/50 bs total=8 fusion.enabled: observed 2-3x p99 variance spikes on ~3% of runs

End-of-log.

(Informal notes style — will refine into a PR checklist and a short confluence summary once experiments finish.)
